stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

on the last line of your reply:

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

# ARC horizontal-tail marker pattern

Use this when a grid has a dominant background color, repeated horizontal motif/stripe rows in another color, and the output introduces color 1.

## Observed rule

Across the demonstrations, the output preserves the input except for the trailing background-colored cells to the right of a selected horizontal stripe/run, which are changed to color 1. The relevant stripe is the lower/repeated instance of the motif (not the upper example/decoy stripe). If the selected stripe reaches the right edge, there is no tail to recolor. Preserve all dimensions and other cells exactly.

Examples supporting the pattern:
- Background 2, stripe color 5: lower stripe row has five 5s followed by three 2s; output changes those three trailing cells to 1.
- Background 3, a near-full horizontal stripe row has a final background cell; output changes that last cell to 1.
- Background 8, repeated motif rows show an open horizontal tail in the lower copy; output marks the background-colored tail in the corresponding row.
- Background 9, stripe color 7: a lower stripe spans 17 cells in a 27-wide grid; change the 10 background cells after it to 1. Leave the upper full-width stripe unchanged.

## Procedure

1. Identify the background color and the repeated non-background horizontal motif/stripe.
2. Compare repeated copies; find the lower/candidate stripe with background-colored cells extending to its right.
3. Change only the contiguous background tail immediately following that run to 1. Do not replace the stripe itself or unrelated background.
4. Maintain exact input dimensions. Before submitting, validate row count, every row width, and values in 0–9; use a small script for long grids to avoid formatting/length errors.
5. If there is ambiguity about which repeated stripe or direction is targeted, request a demonstration rather than guessing; use examples to distinguish a one-cell endpoint from a multi-cell tail.

## Pitfall

A nearly uniform visual grid can make it easy to alter only one tail cell or the wrong stripe. The demonstrated behavior fills the entire trailing segment after the lower target stripe, not merely the first cell after it. Also avoid malformed outputs: generate/validate grids programmatically when dimensions are large.",

Use this when a grid contains repeated horizontal stripe or motif patterns on a solid background, and the demonstrated output marks a terminal background segment using color 1.

## Learned rule from demonstrations

The output retains the input dimensions and nearly all cells. In the relevant repeated/lower motif, change the contiguous background-colored tail at the right edge of the target horizontal run/row to color 1. 1. Identify the background color and the non-background stripe/motif; compare repeated copies to identify the target/lower instance.

5. If the target row or which repeated copy is selected remains uncertain, request a demo instead of guessing.
